title: GH#2: fix npub allowlist and Cloudron startup, add real catalog publishing and runtime smoke
body:
## Summary

Makes the strfry relay package releasable for Cloudron Community Apps (GH#2). Before this PR, the image would crash on Cloudron, `npub` allowlist entries were ignored, and the publish workflow never published anything.

## Defects fixed (each reproduced first)

| Defect | Evidence before | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| strfry exited at startup on Cloudron | Image built from `main`, run with Cloudron's open-file limit (`--ulimit nofile=1024:524288`): `strfry error: Unable to set NOFILES limit to 1000000, exceeds max of 524288`. Hard limit 524288 confirmed in a live app container on the target Cloudron. | `start.sh` sets `relay.nofiles = 0` and raises the soft limit to the hard limit before `gosu`. |
| `npub` allowlist entries never matched | `decode_npub()` expected 52 characters after `npub1`, but an npub has 58. It returned `None` for the NIP-19 test vector. It also ignored the checksum. | Decode per BIP-173 with checksum verification and canonical padding. Tests include the NIP-19 vector plus bad-checksum, uppercase, truncated and wrong-prefix cases. |
| Database capped at 256 MB | `dbParams.mapsize` was set to half the memory limit. In LMDB this is the maximum database size. | Use strfry's default (10 TB of address space, not RAM). |
| Publish workflow was a stub | The `publish` job only printed a message: no image, catalog, tag or release. | Ported the netbird catalog pipeline: GHCR image with provenance, anonymous-pull check, fail-closed `scripts/publish-cloudron-catalog.sh`, catalog attestation, atomic commit+tag push, GitHub release, and idempotent reconcile. |

## Also changed

- **Base image**: builder and runtime both use the digest-pinned `cloudron/base:6.0.0` (Ubuntu 26.04), so strfry links against the runtime's own libraries. Previously it was compiled on Debian bookworm and run on base 5.1.0. The strfry source is pinned to the 1.1.3 tag commit, and the build fails if any shared library is missing (`ldd`).
- **CI runtime smoke** (`test/runtime-smoke.sh`, runs on every PR and before publication): read-only root filesystem, the Cloudron open-file limit, health check `/`, NIP-11 output from app env vars, real WebSocket writes via the pinned `nak` v0.21.2 (sha256-checked), an empty allowlist rejecting writes, an allowlisted npub accepted without a restart, a stranger rejected and not stored, and persistence across a restart.
- **Release credential**: `main` is unprotected, so the catalog push uses the job token. `CLOUDRON_RELEASE_PAT` is used only if it is configured.
- **Listing metadata**: `DESCRIPTION.md`, `iconUrl`, `mediaLinks`, a seeded `CloudronVersions.json`, and removal of the unused `optionalSso`.
- **Docs**: new `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` (NIP-11 env vars); updated allowlist, publishing, packaging notes and README.

## Verification

- `bash test/package-test.sh`, `bash test/relay-smoke.sh`, `bash test/publish-catalog-test.sh`, `actionlint`, `shellcheck`: PASS
- `cloudron-package-helper.sh validate`: PASS
- Local amd64 build on base 6.0.0, then `test/runtime-smoke.sh`: PASS. The same smoke against the `main` image: FAIL (NOFILES abort). This is the negative control.
- PR CI `runtime-smoke`: PASS (run 38988407008)

Live Cloudron qualification (install from the published versions URL, restart, update, backup/restore) follows merge, because merge publishes 0.1.0. Evidence will be recorded on #2 and in `test/QUALIFICATION.md`.

Ref #2

title: GH#2: fix CHANGELOG format for Cloudron catalog publishing
body:
## Summary

The first publication run after #10 (run 38989315752) built, attested and pushed the 0.1.0 image, and passed the anonymous-pull check. It then failed at `cloudron versions add` with `Bad changelog format or missing changelog for this version`. Nothing was written to the catalog, and no tag or release was created.

**Cause:** Cloudron CLI 8.2.6 (`src/helper.js` `parseChangelog`) looks for an exact `[X.Y.Z]` line. `CHANGELOG` used `## [0.1.0] - date`. The package test checked for the Markdown form, and the publisher test stubs the CLI, so neither caught it.

## Changes

- `CHANGELOG`: switched to the Cloudron format (`[0.1.0]` followed by `*` bullets).
- `test/package-test.sh`: the CHANGELOG check now mirrors the CLI parser (an exact header line plus at least one entry before the next `[`).
- `cloudron-catalog-publish.yml` preflight: installs the integrity-pinned Cloudron CLI and runs `cloudron versions add` + `verify` against a scratch copy of the catalog with a placeholder digest. Manifest, DESCRIPTION and CHANGELOG parsing is now checked on every PR, before merge.

## Verification

- With the real CLI 8.2.6, the new CHANGELOG produces a valid `0.1.0` entry with the changelog populated. The old CHANGELOG is rejected by the new package check.
- `bash test/package-test.sh` and `actionlint`: PASS.

Merging this re-runs publication for 0.1.0.

Ref #2

title: GH#2: 0.1.1 post-install guidance and live qualification script
body:
## Summary

0.1.0 is published (#11). It was installed on a live Cloudron from the public versions URL and qualified there. This PR adds 0.1.1, which gives the update-path qualification a real newer version and improves first-run guidance for Community Apps users.

## Changes

- **0.1.1 package UX**
  - `POSTINSTALL.md` (via `postInstallMessage: file://POSTINSTALL.md`) shows the `wss://$CLOUDRON-APP-FQDN` relay URL and how to edit the allowlist from the File Manager or Web Terminal.
  - A manifest `checklist` item reminds the operator to add the first allowlist key.
  - No runtime change.
- **`test/live-qualification.sh`**: repeatable live checks against a disposable app, using throwaway keys only. Its marked allowlist entries are removed on exit.
  - `full [--with-backup-restore]`: NIP-11 env, rejected and accepted writes over `wss://`, restart, then backup and restore with a post-backup write that must roll back.
  - `seed` / `verify-seed`: checks that data survives an app update.
  - The script is covered by the shellcheck run in `test/package-test.sh`.
- **`test/QUALIFICATION.md`**: 0.1.0 live results. The update section is pending until this version publishes.
- **Workflow dry run**: copies every `file://` reference in the manifest instead of a fixed list, and asserts the post-install message resolved.
- **`docs/PUBLISHING.md`**: qualification steps now use the script.

## Verification

- Live, against `relay-test` on 0.1.0: `full --with-backup-restore` passed twice. The restore was a real Cloudron restore task that downloaded and extracted the encrypted backup. `seed` passed, ready for the update check.
- Real Cloudron CLI 8.2.6 `versions add` + `verify` on a scratch catalog: 0.1.1 added with `postInstallMessage`, `checklist` and `changelog` resolved; the catalog is valid (2 versions).
- `bash test/package-test.sh` and `actionlint`: PASS.

Ref #2

title: GH#2: catalog update mode and 0.1.1 live update qualification
body:
## Summary

Completes live qualification of the update path, 0.1.0 → 0.1.1, on a real Cloudron. It also fixes the documented update step, which was wrong.

**What went wrong first:** plain `cloudron update --app relay-test…` run from the repository uploaded the local source and built a `local/com.marcusquinn.cloudron.strfry:0.1.1-…` image on the server, not the published GHCR digest. Cloudron CLI 8.2.6 `update` has no versions-URL option (`src/actions.js` `update()`). That result was discarded: the app was restored from its 0.1.0 pre-update backup, then updated with the published catalog manifest and digest.

## Changes

- `test/live-qualification.sh update-from-catalog <version>`: writes the published catalog manifest (with `dockerImage`) into an empty scratch directory, so the CLI sends it unchanged with a pre-update backup. It then checks that the running image equals the catalog digest, and refuses versions that are not published.
- `docs/PUBLISHING.md`: replaced the incorrect `cloudron update` step, explained the source-build trap, and noted that operators update from the dashboard.
- `test/QUALIFICATION.md`: 0.1.1 and update results, including the discarded attempt. Dashboard update prompts and automatic updates are listed as not covered (Cloudron server behaviour).

## Live evidence (relay-test, my.marcusquinn.com)

- Seeded on 0.1.0 → `update-from-catalog 0.1.1` → `verify-seed`: PASS. The event and allowlist survived, the seeded key still writes, and a stranger key is rejected.
- `full --with-backup-restore` on 0.1.1: PASS.
- Restoring the 0.1.0 backup returned the app to the 0.1.0 catalog image.
- Same-version `update-from-catalog 0.1.1`: PASS; unpublished `9.9.9`: refused.
- `bash test/package-test.sh` (includes shellcheck): PASS.

Ref #2

title: chore: resync framework workflow to aidevops canonical caller
body:
## Summary

Resync `.github/workflows/loc-badge.yml` to the canonical aidevops caller template
(reusable-workflow pattern, GH#20649 + GH#20727).

**Classification before**: `DRIFTED/CALLER`
**Ref**: `@fb06e1b92880fefd839187f8347ae3043b63f3c7`

## Why

The aidevops framework ships managed GitHub Actions workflows as reusable
workflows. Downstream repos carry ~45-line callers that delegate all logic
to the configured aidevops reusable workflow repository/ref.

This PR brings this repo in line with the canonical template, eliminating
drift and unblocking automatic updates when the framework evolves.

## How to verify

After merge, trigger an event matching the workflow triggers. Framework
scripts are fetched at runtime via a secondary checkout — no
`.agents/scripts/` files are needed in this repo.

## Rollback

If the workflow breaks, revert this PR. The previous workflow is preserved
in git history at the parent commit.

Generated by: `aidevops sync-workflows --apply` (see marcusquinn/aidevops#20649).
